findings.highlight: What kind of a person I was like
findings.evidenceJa: 私がどういう人間だったか
findings.governingReading: Saber asks whether Shirou means what sort of person she used to be.
findings.explanation: The English combines two question constructions into one malformed phrase.

findings.highlight: I only emphasized what I was thinking
findings.evidenceJa: 思った事を主張しただけ
findings.governingReading: Saber says she merely stated what she thought.
findings.explanation: “Emphasized” adds rhetorical stress and misses her distinction between asserting a thought and speaking directly from feeling.
